types.embedding_query_text: Person: A human being. Also called Individual, Human, Man, Woman. Examples: Ryan Gosling, Kevin Feige, Josh Horowitz, Shawn Levy.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Person type explicitly includes individual human beings, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional, which perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE and examples.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Audience
candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

types.embedding_query_text: FictionalUniverse: A self-consistent fictional setting where multiple stories, characters, and events exist. Also called Shared World, Story World, Narrative Universe. Examples: Marvel Cinematic Universe, MCU.

chosen_type.label: MovieSeries
chosen_type.justification: The Marvel Cinematic Universe is a prime example of a MovieSeries, which functions as a self-consistent fictional setting for multiple related movies, aligning well with the OIE_TYPE definition.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: ComicStory
candidates.comment: Any indivisible, re-printable unit within a comic, encompassing interior narratives, covers, and backmatter. Also called comic narrative, comic segment, comic content. Examples: The main story in a comic book, a short backup story, a comic book cover, an editorial page. Distinct from ComicCoverArt, which is specifically the artwork on the cover.

candidates.label: ComicSeries
candidates.comment: A sequential publication of comic stories released under a consistent unifying title. Also called comic book series, graphic novel series, comic strip series. Examples: The Walking Dead, Batman, X-Men, Calvin and Hobbes. Distinct from ComicIssue, which is a single installment within the series.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

candidates.label: MovieSeries
candidates.comment: A MovieSeries, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a collection of related movies. Also called film series, movie franchise, film saga. Examples: The Lord of the Rings trilogy, the James Bond film series, the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Distinct from MovieClip, which is a short segment of a single movie.

types.embedding_query_text: Year: A period of 365 or 366 days, typically from January 1 to December 31. Also called Calendar Year, Annum. Examples: 2028, 2026, last year, 1967.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.definition: The length of time that something continues or lasts.
chosen_type.justification: A year is a specific period of time, and 'last year' is a qualitative duration, both fitting the schema.org Duration type.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

types.embedding_query_text: FictionalCharacter: An imaginary person or entity in a fictional work. Also called Character, Role, Persona. Examples: Ghost Rider, Carter Slade, Johnny Blaze, Satan.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Person type explicitly includes fictional characters, which perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE and examples.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason

candidates.label: Play
candidates.comment: A Play is a CreativeWork in the form of literature, primarily consisting of dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance. Also called stage play, drama, theatrical work. Examples: "Hamlet", "Death of a Salesman", "Hamilton", "A Streetcar Named Desire". Distinct from TheaterEvent, which is the actual performance of a play.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a particular purpose. Also called Company, Corporation, Agency, Group. Examples: Marvel, Marvel Studios.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: Marvel (e.g., Marvel Entertainment, Marvel Studios) is a group of people with a particular purpose, which is a direct match for schema.org Organization.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

types.embedding_query_text: Convention: A large meeting or assembly, typically of members of a profession or group, to discuss common interests. Also called Conference, Gathering, Summit, Expo. Examples: San Diego Comic-Con, the comic book convention.

chosen_type.label: ConferenceEvent
chosen_type.justification: San Diego Comic-Con is a well-known convention, which is explicitly covered by the schema.org ConferenceEvent type.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: BusinessEvent
candidates.comment: A BusinessEvent is an Event related to commercial activities, such as conferences, trade shows, or corporate meetings. Also called corporate event, professional gathering, industry event. Examples: a sales conference, a product launch event, an annual shareholder meeting. Distinct from SocialEvent, which is for personal or recreational gatherings.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

types.embedding_query_text: DayOfWeek: One of the seven named days that make up a week. Also called Weekday, Weekend Day. Examples: Sunday.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org DayOfWeek enumeration is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE and the example 'Sunday'.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

types.embedding_query_text: Group: A number of people or things that are located, gathered, or classed together. Also called Collective, Assembly, Crowd, Team. Examples: fans, audience, crowd, Marvel fans.

chosen_type.label: Audience
chosen_type.justification: The mentions 'fans', 'audience', and 'crowd' all refer to groups of people for whom creative work is intended or who are spectators, which aligns with schema.org Audience.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Consortium

Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

types.embedding_query_text: FanDemand: A request or strong desire expressed by a group of enthusiasts or supporters. Also called Fan Request, Public Demand, Audience Expectation. Examples: fans’ demands.

chosen_type.label: Demand
chosen_type.justification: FanDemand is a specific type of request or strong desire, which is best represented by the broader schema.org Demand type for seeking goods or services.

candidates.label: Demand
candidates.comment: An intangible entity representing a public announcement by an organization or person seeking specific goods or services. Also called Request for goods, wanted ad, procurement request, call for bids. Examples: A company seeking bids for a new IT system, a person looking to buy a specific vintage car, a job posting for a software engineer. Distinct from Offer, which is an announcement to provide goods or services.

candidates.label: WantAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a desire or wish for an object or outcome. Also called desire, wish for, covet. Examples: wanting a new car, desiring a specific job, wishing for peace.

candidates.label: Audience
candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

candidates.label: OnDemandEvent
candidates.comment: An OnDemandEvent, as a PublicationEvent, is a publication event where a program is available on-demand. Also called catch-up TV, podcast release, streaming event. Examples: a TV show episode available for streaming after broadcast, a podcast episode release, a movie available for rent online. Distinct from BroadcastEvent, which is a live or scheduled transmission.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

types.embedding_query_text: Object: A material thing that can be seen and touched. Also called Item, Thing, Device, Article. Examples: microphone, screen.

chosen_type.label: Thing
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'Object' and examples 'microphone', 'screen' are general physical items, for which schema.org Thing is the most appropriate generic type when no more specific type fits.

candidates.label: ImageObject
candidates.comment: An ImageObject is a media object creative work representing an image file. Also called picture, photo, graphic, visual. Examples: a JPEG photograph, a PNG illustration, a GIF animation. Distinct from VideoObject, which is a video file, and AudioObject, which is an audio file.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: VideoObject
candidates.comment: A media object representing a video file. Also called video file, digital video, movie clip. Examples: an MP4 video, a YouTube video, a short film.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: AudioObject
candidates.comment: An AudioObject is a MediaObject representing an audio file or recording. Also called audio file, sound recording, sound clip, audio track. Examples: an MP3 song, a podcast episode, a voice memo, a sound effect. Distinct from VideoObject, which contains visual content.

types.embedding_query_text: Concept: An abstract idea or general notion. Also called Idea, Notion, Abstraction. Examples: dream casting.

chosen_type.label: Concept
chosen_type.definition: An abstract idea or general notion.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type adequately represents an abstract idea or general notion like 'dream casting'; therefore, a new type is minted with Thing as its parent.

candidates.label: DefinedTermSet
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a collection of formally defined terms, such as a glossary, dictionary, or classification scheme. Also called Glossary, vocabulary, taxonomy, thesaurus, enumeration. Examples: The Dewey Decimal Classification system, a medical dictionary, a list of product categories, a set of industry standards. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a single entry within such a set.

candidates.label: CreativeWork
candidates.comment: A CreativeWork is the most generic type of intellectual or artistic creation, encompassing a wide range of media and forms. Also called artistic work, intellectual property, creation, content. Examples: A novel, a film, a photograph, a piece of software, a song, a painting.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: Clip
candidates.comment: A short segment or part of a larger audio or video program. Also called segment, excerpt, snippet, short video. Examples: A news clip, a movie trailer, a highlight reel from a sports game, a sound bite. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is the broader category for any creative content.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

types.embedding_query_text: Duration: The length of time that something continues or exists. Also called Period, Span, Length of Time. Examples: years, a very long time.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.definition: The length of time that something continues or lasts.
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Duration type directly represents a period of time, which is a perfect match for the OIE_TYPE and examples like 'years' and 'a very long time'.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

types.embedding_query_text: PanelDiscussion: A public discussion in which a group of experts or notable figures discuss a topic in front of an audience. Also called Panel, Forum, Roundtable. Examples: panel.

candidates.label: EventAttendanceModeEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EventAttendanceModeEnumeration is an Enumeration of modes for organizing an event, indicating whether it is online or offline. candidates.label: TaxiStand
candidates.comment: A civic structure or designated area where taxis wait for passengers. Also called cab stand, taxi rank, hack stand. Examples: a taxi stand at an airport, a designated taxi area outside a hotel, a street corner taxi queue.

candidates.label: ScreeningEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving the public showing of a movie or other video content. Also called film screening, movie showing, video presentation, cinema event. Examples: a film festival screening, a premiere showing of a new movie, a public documentary viewing, a drive-in movie night.

types.embedding_query_text: Location: A place or position. Also called Place, Site, Venue, Spot. Examples: hall, stage.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Place type represents an entity with a fixed physical extension, which perfectly describes 'hall' and 'stage' as locations.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: Seat
candidates.comment: A specific seating location, often reserved, within an event venue or transportation. Also called reserved spot, seating assignment, chair, place. Examples: seat 12A on an airplane, row F seat 5 at a concert, a specific table at a restaurant.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: Room
candidates.comment: A distinguishable space within a structure, typically separated by interior walls. Also called chamber, compartment, space, area. Examples: a hotel room, a living room, a bedroom, a conference room.

types.embedding_query_text: Music: Vocal or instrumental sounds combined in such a way as to produce beauty of form, harmony, and expression of emotion. Also called Soundtrack, Score, Melody. Examples: pounding bass soundtrack.

chosen_type.label: MusicRecording
chosen_type.justification: The mention 'pounding bass soundtrack' refers to recorded music, which is best represented by schema.org MusicRecording, a recorded performance of a musical composition.

candidates.label: SheetMusic
candidates.comment: Printed or written musical notation, as distinct from a performance or recording. Also called musical score, notation, music manuscript, song sheet. Examples: a piano concerto score, guitar tablature, a vocal sheet for a song, an orchestral score.

candidates.label: MusicComposition
candidates.comment: A MusicComposition is a musical work, such as a song or symphony, that can be performed or recorded. Also called musical piece, song, score. Examples: Beethoven's 5th Symphony, 'Bohemian Rhapsody' by Queen, a jingle. Distinct from MusicRecording, which is a recorded performance of a composition.

candidates.label: MusicAlbum
candidates.comment: A MusicAlbum, as a MusicPlaylist, is a collection of music tracks released together. Also called album, record album, studio album. Examples: 'Thriller' by Michael Jackson, 'Abbey Road' by The Beatles, a compilation album. Distinct from MusicRecording, which is usually a single song.

candidates.label: MusicRecording
candidates.comment: A MusicRecording, as a CreativeWork, is a recorded performance of a musical composition, usually a single song. Also called music track, song recording, audio track. Examples: 'Yesterday' by The Beatles (the recorded version), a single from an album, a demo track. Distinct from MusicComposition, which is the abstract musical work.

candidates.label: MusicAlbumProductionType
candidates.comment: MusicAlbumProductionType is an enumeration classifying a music album by its content type. Also called album type, production category. Examples: StudioAlbum, LiveAlbum, Soundtrack, CompilationAlbum. Distinct from MusicAlbumReleaseType, which describes the release format.

types.embedding_query_text: TextDisplay: A visual presentation of text, often on a screen or surface. Also called Text Projection, Visual Text, Displayed Words. Examples: “Ghost Rider”, the words “Ghost Rider”.

chosen_type.label: TextDisplay
chosen_type.definition: A visual presentation of text, often on a screen or surface.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type specifically captures the concept of a visual presentation of text on a screen or surface; therefore, a new type is minted with Thing as its parent.

candidates.label: PronounceableText

candidates.label: TextDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A digital document primarily composed of textual content. Also called text file, digital document, e-document. Examples: a PDF report, a Word document, an e-book. Distinct from TextObject, which is a media object representing a text file, often for embedding or linking.

candidates.label: PresentationDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A PresentationDigitalDocument is a DigitalDocument file containing slides or used for a presentation. Also called slide deck, presentation file, slideshow. Examples: a Microsoft PowerPoint file, a Google Slides presentation, a Keynote document, a PDF of presentation slides.

candidates.label: Text
candidates.comment: A fundamental data type representing a sequence of characters. Also called string, character data, plain text. Examples: "Hello World", "123 Main St", "product description".

candidates.label: ScreeningEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving the public showing of a movie or other video content. Also called film screening, movie showing, video presentation, cinema event. Examples: a film festival screening, a premiere showing of a new movie, a public documentary viewing, a drive-in movie night.

chosen_type.label: ReactAction

candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

candidates.label: DislikeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative sentiment or disapproval towards an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express dislike, disapprove of, show aversion, downvote. Examples: Disliking a movie, expressing disapproval of a policy, downvoting a comment online. Distinct from LikeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or approval.

candidates.label: EducationalAudience
candidates.comment: An EducationalAudience is an Audience specifically targeted for educational content or programs. Also called student group, learner demographic, academic audience. Examples: K-12 students, university undergraduates, adult learners, professional development participants.

candidates.label: ReactAction
candidates.comment: ReactAction is an AssessAction representing the act of responding instinctively and emotionally to an object, expressing a sentiment. Also called emotional response, sentiment expression. Examples: liking a social media post, disliking a video, expressing shock at news, showing approval for an idea.

types.embedding_query_text: Film: A motion picture or movie. Also called Movie, Motion Picture, Cinema. Examples: Star Wars: Starfighter.

chosen_type.label: Movie
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Movie type is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE 'Film' and the example 'Star Wars: Starfighter'.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: MovieTheater
candidates.comment: A MovieTheater is a civic structure designed for public viewing of movies. Also called cinema, picture house, movie house. Examples: AMC Theatres, local independent cinema, drive-in movie theater. Distinct from MovieRentalStore, which is a business for renting movies.

candidates.label: MovieSeries
candidates.comment: A MovieSeries, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a collection of related movies. Also called film series, movie franchise, film saga. Examples: The Lord of the Rings trilogy, the James Bond film series, the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Distinct from MovieClip, which is a short segment of a single movie.

candidates.label: ScreeningEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving the public showing of a movie or other video content. Also called film screening, movie showing, video presentation, cinema event. Examples: a film festival screening, a premiere showing of a new movie, a public documentary viewing, a drive-in movie night.

candidates.label: FilmAction
candidates.comment: FilmAction is a CreateAction representing the act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally. Also called shooting a film, recording video, filming. Examples: Filming a movie scene, recording a documentary, shooting a wedding video, capturing a short clip on a phone.

types.embedding_query_text: Award: A prize or other mark of recognition given in honor of an achievement. Also called Prize, Honor, Accolade, Trophy. Examples: Golden Globe.

chosen_type.label: Certification
chosen_type.justification: A 'Golden Globe' is an official mark of recognition for achievement, which can be considered a form of certification of excellence, making schema.org Certification the best fit among candidates.

candidates.label: WinAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving victory or success in a competitive activity. Also called triumph, succeed, prevail. Examples: winning a race, winning a championship, winning an argument.

candidates.label: Certification
candidates.comment: An official and authoritative statement attesting to specific characteristics of a subject, issued by an independent body. Also called accreditation, credential, attestation, endorsement. Examples: ISO 9001 certification, Organic food certification, PMP certification, LEED certification.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: EndorsementRating
candidates.comment: An EndorsementRating is a Rating that expresses a positive level of endorsement, such as a "critic's pick" or a social media "Like," often without a numeric scale. Also called positive rating, approval rating, recommendation. Examples: A "thumbs up" icon, a "recommended by critics" badge, a social media "Like" count, inclusion in a "best of" list.

types.embedding_query_text: FilmProduction: The process of making a film, from initial concept to final cut. Also called Filming, Movie Making, Production. Examples: shooting “Star Wars: Starfighter”.

chosen_type.label: FilmAction
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'FilmProduction' and the example 'shooting 'Star Wars: Starfighter'' directly align with schema.org FilmAction, which represents the act of capturing moving images.

candidates.label: FilmAction
candidates.comment: FilmAction is a CreateAction representing the act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally. Also called shooting a film, recording video, filming. Examples: Filming a movie scene, recording a documentary, shooting a wedding video, capturing a short clip on a phone.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: CreateAction
candidates.comment: A CreateAction is the act of deliberately producing, generating, or building a new result or entity by an agent. Also called production, generation, fabrication, construction. Examples: Writing a book, composing a song, building a house, designing a website.

candidates.label: MovieSeries
candidates.comment: A MovieSeries, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a collection of related movies. Also called film series, movie franchise, film saga. Examples: The Lord of the Rings trilogy, the James Bond film series, the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Distinct from MovieClip, which is a short segment of a single movie.

types.embedding_query_text: CharacterArchetype: A typical example of a person or thing, often recurring in literature or mythology. Also called Archetype, Stock Character, Stereotype. Examples: Western hero, the “world’s most mysterious Western hero”.

chosen_type.label: CharacterArchetype
chosen_type.definition: A typical example of a person or thing, often recurring in literature or mythology.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type adequately represents a recurring character type like 'Western hero'; therefore, a new type is minted with Thing as its parent.

candidates.label: CarUsageType
candidates.comment: An enumeration indicating a specific purpose or usage of a car. Also called vehicle use category, automobile purpose, car application type. Examples: Commercial rental, driving school, taxi service, personal use.

candidates.label: BoardingPolicyType
candidates.comment: An Enumeration representing different policies used by airlines for boarding passengers. Also called airline boarding rule, boarding group type, flight boarding policy. Examples: "Zone boarding", "Group boarding", "Priority boarding", "Family boarding".

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: PaymentMethodType
candidates.comment: PaymentMethodType is an enumeration for generic types of payment methods. Also called payment category, payment classification. Examples: CreditCard, DebitCard, BankTransfer, Cash. Distinct from PaymentMethod, which can be a specific instance or a broader concept.

candidates.label: MapCategoryType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of different categories or kinds of maps. Also called map type, map classification, cartography category. Examples: "RoadMap", "SatelliteMap", "TerrainMap", "HybridMap".

types.embedding_query_text: ComicBookIssue: A single published installment of a comic book series. Also called Comic Issue, Graphic Novel Issue. Examples: Marvel Spotlight issue 5.

chosen_type.label: ComicIssue
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org ComicIssue type is a direct and perfect match for a single published installment of a comic book series, as exemplified by 'Marvel Spotlight issue 5'.

candidates.label: ComicIssue
candidates.comment: An individual, serially published installment of a comic series, uniquely identified by its series name, volume, issue number, and variant description. Also called comic book, comic installment, single issue comic. Examples: The Amazing Spider-Man #1, Detective Comics Vol. 2 #27, Saga #50, a one-shot comic. Distinct from ComicSeries, which is the overarching publication title.

candidates.label: PublicationIssue
candidates.comment: A PublicationIssue is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or publication volume, often numbered and containing a grouping of works. Also called journal issue, magazine issue, periodical issue. Examples: "Nature" Vol. 500, Issue 1; "The New Yorker" October 26, 2023 issue; a specific issue of a scientific journal. Distinct from PublicationVolume, which is a larger grouping of issues.

candidates.label: ComicCoverArt
candidates.comment: The visual artwork specifically featured on the cover of a comic book or issue. Also called comic book cover, graphic novel cover, comic art. Examples: The cover of Action Comics #1, a variant cover for a Marvel comic, a graphic novel's front illustration. Distinct from ComicStory, which refers to any indivisible, re-printable unit of a comic, including interior stories.

candidates.label: ComicSeries
candidates.comment: A sequential publication of comic stories released under a consistent unifying title. Also called comic book series, graphic novel series, comic strip series. Examples: The Walking Dead, Batman, X-Men, Calvin and Hobbes. Distinct from ComicIssue, which is a single installment within the series.

candidates.label: PublicationVolume
candidates.comment: A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume. Examples: "Nature" Volume 500; "Encyclopedia Britannica" Volume 1; a year's collection of a magazine. Distinct from PublicationIssue, which is a smaller, more granular part of a volume.

types.embedding_query_text: LovedOne: A person one loves or is very fond of. Also called Dear One, Beloved, Family Member, Partner. Examples: someone he loves.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: A 'loved one' is an individual human being, which is directly covered by the schema.org Person type.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: EmployeeRole
candidates.comment: An EmployeeRole is an OrganizationRole describing the relationship of an individual as an employee within an organization. Also called job position, staff role, employment status. Examples: "Software Engineer" at Google, "Marketing Manager" at a startup, "Cashier" at a supermarket.

candidates.label: MusicVenue
candidates.comment: A MusicVenue is a civic structure or place specifically designed for musical performances. Also called concert hall, live music venue, performance space. Examples: Carnegie Hall, a local bar with live bands, an outdoor amphitheater. Distinct from MovieTheater, which is for film screenings.

candidates.label: LikeAction
candidates.comment: A LikeAction is a react action representing the act of expressing a positive sentiment about an object. Also called approve action, endorse action, favorite action. Examples: liking a post on social media, giving a thumbs-up to a video, expressing approval for an idea. Distinct from DislikeAction, which expresses negative sentiment.

types.embedding_query_text: FictionalElement: A component or aspect that exists within a fictional narrative or world. Also called Fictional Concept, Story Element, Imaginary Component. Examples: hellfire, flaming skull.

chosen_type.label: FictionalElement
chosen_type.definition: A component or aspect that exists within a fictional narrative or world.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type adequately represents a component within a fictional narrative like 'hellfire' or 'flaming skull'; therefore, a new type is minted with Thing as its parent.

candidates.label: WebPageElement
candidates.comment: A distinct part or component within a web page. Also called page component, web element, UI element. Examples: a navigation menu, an image, a form, a table.

candidates.label: ArchiveComponent
candidates.comment: An ArchiveComponent is an intangible CreativeWork representing any content within an archive, whether an individual item or a collection, described by specific archival properties. Also called archival item, archival record, archive content, collection item. Examples: a historical letter, a collection of photographs, a government document series, a digital archive file.

candidates.label: SiteNavigationElement
candidates.comment: A web page element that provides navigation links or controls for a website. Also called navigation menu, website menu, nav bar, site map. Examples: the main menu bar at the top of a website, a sidebar navigation, a footer navigation.

candidates.label: Episode
candidates.comment: An Episode is a CreativeWork representing a single installment of a media series, such as a TV show, radio program, or video game. Also called installment, segment, part. Examples: A single episode of a TV series, a chapter in a podcast, a level in a video game series.

candidates.label: WPSideBar
candidates.comment: A section of a web page positioned to the side of the main content, often used for navigation, advertisements, or supplementary information. Also called page sidebar, side panel, auxiliary column. Examples: a navigation menu on the left side of a blog, a list of related articles in a right sidebar, an ad column.

types.embedding_query_text: JobTitle: The name of a position held by an individual within an organization. Also called Position, Role, Designation. Examples: President.

chosen_type.label: OrganizationRole
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org OrganizationRole type directly describes a specific function or position within an organization, which is a perfect match for 'JobTitle' and the example 'President'.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: EmployeeRole
candidates.comment: An EmployeeRole is an OrganizationRole describing the relationship of an individual as an employee within an organization. Also called job position, staff role, employment status. Examples: "Software Engineer" at Google, "Marketing Manager" at a startup, "Cashier" at a supermarket.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: JobPosting
candidates.comment: A JobPosting is an intangible listing that describes an open position within an organization. Also called job advertisement, employment listing, career opening. Examples: a software engineer job posting, a marketing manager vacancy, a retail associate opening.
